REPRO (VERIFIED, artifacts/review-w05-02/reviewer-floor-rollback-probe.test.ts, log https://la-hacks-rttothemoon.devinenterprise.com/attachments/087e11ec-bb50-4fb5-a8b5-44c7068354e6/reviewer-floor-rollback-probe.log): anchor at SERVER_MS, checkpoint at +3d, relaunch with wall at +6d -> read() nowMs=+6d, evaluateLease(7-day lease) active remainingMs=1d; then wind the wall clock back 3 days (monotonic advances 1h) -> read() nowMs=+3d, rollbackDetected=false, evaluateLease active remainingMs=345600000 (4d). The lease was extended by 3 days by a backwards wall-clock jump, undetected. Because the floor is never re-persisted without an anchor, the second probe test shows a device that relaunches 30 times with the wall clock reset to the floor each time keeps the lease 'active' 33 days after issue (7-day cap never reached). Fix inside write_paths: in floor mode, pin the first reading to the monotonic clock (treat max(floor, adjustedWall) at monotonic t0 as an in-process anchor so later reads are >= that + monotonic elapsed and a lower adjusted wall clock is a rollback), and checkpoint the in-process high-water mark to the Keychain in floor mode too; add tests for both scenarios (they must fail on base and pass on the candidate).

Low risk because the response still comes from the real origin over TLS, but the module's contract says 'only responses to bearer-authenticated requests are trusted'.
